title: Machine-learning models identify cerebrospinal-fluid protein signatures for multiple-sclerosis activity and disability progression
summary: Using Olink proteomics of 1,463 proteins in CSF and plasma from two prospective Swedish cohorts, the study trained prediction models for multiple-sclerosis diagnosis, 2-year disease activity and long-term disability worsening. Lower CSF neurofilament light (NfL) predicted absence of disease activity at two years (replication AUC 0.77). A stepwise model using 11 CSF proteins (CXCL13, LTA, FCN2, ICAM3, LY9, SLAMF7, TYMP, CHI3L1, FYB1, TNFRSF1B and NfL) predicted normalized age-related MS severity; subgroup classification AUCs in the replication cohort ranged from 0.88 to 0.90.
ai_technology: Stepwise logistic regression for diagnosis and disease activity; stepwise linear regression for long-term disability severity
organization: Linköping University; University of Skövde; Karolinska Institutet and Karolinska University Hospital; collaborating Swedish institutions

evidence.tested: Using Olink proteomics of 1,463 proteins in CSF and plasma from two prospective Swedish cohorts, the study trained prediction models for multiple-sclerosis diagnosis, 2-year disease activity and long-term disability worsening.
evidence.unknown: The study included 143 people with early-stage MS and 43 healthy controls across discovery and replication cohorts; the replication MS cohort had 51 participants. The 2-year disease-activity comparison in replication was especially small (45 with activity versus 5 without). The 11-protein severity model predicted observational disability scores rather than treatment benefit. The plasma severity model had only 12 eligible replication samples and performed less convincingly. These are cohort-level results, not a clinically validated diagnostic assay or independent replication by another research group.
evidence.ai_role: The study used statistical differential-expression testing to select disease-associated candidate proteins, then fitted logistic-regression models to predict MS diagnosis and 2-year disease activity and a linear-regression model to predict long-term normalized age-related MS severity. Stepwise feature selection produced the protein combinations; the frozen models were evaluated in a separate prospective cohort.
